answer.rationale: The scenario describes a near-miss that could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic release of a highly hazardous chemical at a PSM-covered process. This directly triggers the incident investigation requirement under 1910.119(m)(1), which mandates investigation of incidents that resulted in or could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic release, regardless of whether an injury occurred. No fatality, hospitalization, amputation, or loss of eye is reported, so OSHA recordkeeping reporting thresholds (1904.39) are not triggered. Contractor-related PSM provisions are not clearly implicated since no contractor-specific hazard exposure or injury is described.
